picks.title: Vibe coding is turning the music gear world upside down
picks.rationale: LLM coding assistants are letting ordinary users write custom firmware and hacks for synths, samplers and grooveboxes. That changes who gets to reshape hardware instruments. The angle is hardware hacking, not the vibe-coded plugin market covered on 10-17.
picks.excerpt: LLM coding assistants have triggered an explosion of user-built custom firmware and hacks for synths, samplers and grooveboxes, changing who gets to reshape music hardware.

picks.title: Artists Behind Olivia Rodrigo 'Expectations' Music Video Debunk AI Accusations
picks.rationale: A graphic designer released behind-the-scenes process footage (2D/3D animation, analog treatments) to answer claims the video was AI-made. Publishing process as proof of human work is a direct lesson for visual creatives.
picks.excerpt: Graphic designer Jack Harrison and Rodrigo's official fan account released behind-the-scenes footage of the 2D/3D animation and analog treatments to rebut claims the video was AI-generated.

picks.title: Sony and Universal ask court to force Suno investor Lightspeed to testify about the 'legal risk of training data'
picks.rationale: This is a new court filing (Oct 13, Boston federal court) in the labels' Suno case. It pushes discovery onto a VC investor's own assessment of the risk in Suno's training data, which raises the stakes for anyone funding generative music models.
picks.excerpt: In a Boston federal court filing on October 13, Sony and Universal opposed Suno investor Lightspeed's motion to quash their subpoena seeking testimony on the 'legal risk of training data'.

picks.title: The three big debates around music and generative AI
picks.rationale: CMU organises the generative-music fight into three debates: training consent, licensing and output. It is a useful map of where the industry argument stands, written ahead of its Un-Convention panel.
picks.excerpt: Generative AI models that output music pose many questions for the industry; CMU organises them into three big debates ahead of an Un-Convention panel on music and AI.

picks.title: D-Composer: Language Modeling for Simultaneous Drum Transcription and Sound Event Decomposition
picks.rationale: This model transcribes a drum part and splits it back into its one-shot samples in a single pass. That points to tools that can rebuild a kit and its pattern from any recorded beat.
picks.excerpt: D-Composer uses language modelling to transcribe drum beats while decomposing them into their constituent one-shot sound events, building on drum analysis-by-synthesis models.
